criteria.criterion: In crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs, STEWARD_PROMPT tells the steward to step back (look across repeated failures and blind spots for the root cause) and to decide and queue a request itself. It limits a brief for the owner to an environment change or a token or credential Athena needs. Check with Grep/Read of the diff.
criteria.evidence: I read roles.rs lines 120-129. The prompt says "Step back: look across repeated failures and blind spots for the root cause", "Decide the fix yourself: for a rung at or below your limit, write a request and Athena queues it. Do not ask the owner to decide." and "Write a brief for the owner only when Athena needs an environment change or a token or credential (for example a missing GH_TOKEN)."

criteria.criterion: The steward prompt no longer asks for an owner brief on any other kind of proposal, and the 'Your report' / 'Your limit' text in crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs agrees with the prompt. Check by reading the diff.
criteria.evidence: The old sentence "For a proposal above your limit, also write a brief for the owner" is removed. The prompt now ends with "Leave the brief null for every other item." In steward.rs (diff at lines 1035-1040 and 1082-1087), "Your limit" adds "write a `brief` for the owner only when Athena needs an environment change or a token or credential, and leave it null for every other item", and "Your report" adds "Give a `brief` only for an environment change or a token or credential Athena needs." The three texts agree.

findings.summary: The env/token exception, the one case the owner wants to be asked about, never reaches the owner as a brief
findings.evidence: `decide()` keeps `change.brief` only for `Decision::Proposed` (rung above the limit) and drops it for `Applied`. The prompt says to write a brief for an environment change or a token, but never tells the steward to rank such an item above its limit. The prompt's own example, a missing GH_TOKEN, shows up as an unreadable `gh` source. `blind_spot_change` hard-codes that at `Ladder::Implementation` with `brief: None`, so it becomes a queued request and the owner is never asked. A sounder approach makes env/token needs a distinct item kind, or routes them to the owner whatever the rung.

findings.summary: Proposals above the limit still go to the owner, now without a brief
findings.evidence: `open_proposals` lists every Proposal work item that has no decision, whether or not it has a brief. After this change, a design-rung proposal the steward raises still lands on the owner as an open decision. The prompt now forbids the brief, so the owner gets the same decision with less to go on. That is the opposite of "I don't want decisions". The reading kept this route, but the result does not cut the decisions that reach the owner.

findings.summary: The reading does not match the request, so passing criteria do not show the request was met
findings.evidence: The owner wants to be asked only about environment changes or tokens. The reading keeps the existing route, where every proposal above the steward's rung becomes an open proposal for the owner, and changes only whether that proposal has a brief. So the owner is still sent non-env/token decisions; they just arrive without the plain-language brief. The reverse case also fails. The code keeps a brief only on items above the steward's limit, and a missing-GH_TOKEN blind spot sits on the lowest rung, so the one kind of decision the owner wants never reaches them as a brief.

summary: The change rewrites STEWARD_PROMPT and the steward's "Your limit" and "Your report" text so the steward steps back, decides fixes itself, and writes an owner brief only for an environment change or a token. It bumps the role to version 3 and documents the rule as prose-only. The text changes are coherent and the targeted tests pass. The verdict is still fail, for three reasons. (1) There is no test that an item needing an environment change or token keeps its brief while other items get none, so criterion 3 is unmet; crates/athena-cli/tests/steward.rs, a listed deliverable, was not changed. (2) No test measures the real prompt against the 600-token steward budget; the check_budget test uses a placeholder string. Counting the source bytes by hand puts the composed prompt at about 634 tokens, over the 600 budget. This is an estimate, not a measurement. (3) The approach does not deliver the request. `decide()` keeps a brief only for proposals above the steward's limit, while env/token needs such as a missing GH_TOKEN land on low rungs where the brief is dropped. Meanwhile, proposals above the limit still reach the owner as open decisions, now without a brief.
